---
title: "Prepare patient histories"
description: "Prepare Cohort2Trajectory output or local interval rows for transition and cost analysis."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis)
invisible(capture.output(source(system.file(
  "examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"
), local = TRUE)))
```

`prepareTrajectories()` validates interval rows and records the state dictionary,
cycle length and observation boundaries used by later analyses.

The examples use synthetic data from the
[quickstart script](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/quickstart.R).
To load the same objects in R:

```{r load-example, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"))
```

## Supply the interval columns

A local data frame needs these four columns. Dates include both endpoints.

| Column | Meaning |
|:--|:--|
| `subject_id` | Patient identifier. Preserve large or zero-prefixed IDs as text. |
| `state_label` | Clinical state for the interval. |
| `state_start_date` | First observed date in the state. |
| `state_end_date` | Last observed date in the state. |

```{r prepare}
histories <- prepareTrajectories(
  trajectories, cycleLength = 7,
  states = c("Stable", "Complication", "Dead"), absorbingStates = "Dead"
)
histories
```

`cycleLength` is needed for discrete transition and occupancy analyses. It can
remain `NULL` for interval-based cost estimation. `states` is optional when the
observed labels cover the intended dictionary; supply it to include unobserved
states or choose their order. Declare absorbing states explicitly.

Extra columns, such as birth date or treatment status, are preserved. Preparation
does not infer clinical states or validate allowed-transition rules from C2T.

## Use Cohort2Trajectory output

C2T's default `targetEpisodeHandling = "First"` output carries a
`trajectory_definition` attribute. It supplies omitted cycle length, ordered
states and absorbing states. Explicit arguments must agree with it.

For your own first-episode output:

```{r c2t-input, eval=FALSE}
histories <- prepareTrajectories(c2t_output)
saveRDS(c2t_output, "trajectories.rds")
```

RDS preserves the definition; CSV does not. After importing a CSV, supply the
model definitions explicitly as in the local-data example.

C2T's `"All"` mode uses version 2 metadata and patient–episode identity. TMA
currently supports one target episode per patient. Use `"First"` output for
this workflow; do not remove episode metadata to combine episodes into one
patient history.

## Check boundaries and unresolved intervals

`START` and `EXIT` are observation markers. `OUT OF COHORT` is an unresolved
interval. None belongs in the clinical state dictionary.

Preparation rejects duplicate intervals, overlaps and leaving a declared
absorbing state. With a cycle length, starts must align with the patient's
index date and only the final observed cycle may be short. Each patient needs
at least one observed interval.

Without boundary markers, TMA uses the first and last observed intervals.
Those dates cannot independently verify the original observation window.

```{r inspect-boundaries}
histories$patients
histories$diagnostics
```

## Define groups before estimation

Numeric strata use exact values. Make age bands explicitly when that is the
intended analysis. Groups include the lower boundary and exclude the upper.

```{r group-covariates}
rows <- trajectories
rows$birth_date <- as.Date("1961-01-08")
groups <- list(age_group = list(
  column = "age", breaks = c(0, 65, Inf), labels = c("Under 65", "65+")
))
grouped_rows <- addCovariateGroups(rows, groups, dateColumn = "state_start_date")
head(grouped_rows[c("subject_id", "state_start_date", "age", "age_group")], 4)
```

With dates, age is completed calendar years at the row's start. This helper
does not split an interval at a birthday. Covariates must represent information
available at the start of each source interval.
